long_biography.plain_text:
Real-time enterprise software was the idea Hasso Plattner and four fellow IBM engineers pursued when they established SAP. As chief executive, he kept product development at the centre of the company and helped turn a single-product German venture into a global enterprise-applications group. Years later, work with students at the Hasso Plattner Institute contributed to SAP HANA, an in-memory database system.

Plattner founded the Potsdam institute in 1998 as a privately funded centre for digital engineering. He headed its Enterprise Platform and Integration Concepts research group and taught until 2023. The institute now operates with the University of Potsdam's Digital Engineering Faculty under the sole shareholding of the Hasso Plattner Foundation, preserving a permanent institution for computing research and teaching.

The SEC filing establishes the last reviewed exact personal holding and clearly separates foundation-owned shares, but the dossier deliberately omits a percentage because Plattner is below SAP's current major-shareholder disclosure table and the figure can change.
